newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein firmer, demand improves.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein firmer, demand improves.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were firmer in late trading on Wednesday, with demand improving following gains in Malaysia, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,415-20 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, up from 1,410-15 rupiah at the opening. Crude palm oil was done at 1,170 rupiah/kg at a 1000-tonne tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan, unchanged from the previous tender.

"The market was a little better today, with prices edging up following increases in Malaysia," one trader said. "Some local sellers withdrew from the market after prices in Malaysia went up, on anticipation of further gains in the local market."
But Malaysian prices eased towards the close because the fundamentals there are considered weak, he added.
Traders said Indonesian palm olein export prices were at a premium to local values while crude palm oil fetched a better price in the local market.
"The export price for palm olein is still at a premium to local prices, but it is the reverse for crude palm oil," one said. "It is good news for refiners."

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MV Hanjani will sail for Malaysia's Pasir Gudang on Wednesday with 1,375 tonnes of coconut oil. The MV Beatrice will said for Japan on Thursday with 1,000 tonnes of crude palm oil.
The MT Pan Oil-6 will leave for Tanjung Priok on Thursday with 3,200 tonnes of palm kernel oil.
